paper.title: Low-density Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high entropy steel processed by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering: Phase evolution, microstructure and mechanical properties
keywords: Mechanical milling and spark plasma sintering
paper.paper_scope: Synthesis and characterization of a novel non-equiatomic low-density Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high entropy steel prepared by 35 h mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering, systematically studying phase evolution with milling time, thermal stability by annealing (400-800 °C), resulting microstructure (BCC + B2 + gamma-brass + Fe5Si3 silicide) and mechanical properties (microhardness, elastic modulus, compressive strength) correlated with thermodynamic parameters, CALPHAD predictions and strengthening mechanisms.

aliases: Fe Mn Ni Al Si C high entropy steel
alloys.description: Novel non-equiatomic low-density high entropy steel (HES) designed to form a multi-phase microstructure (mainly BCC ferrite as major phase plus partially ordered B2) for high mechanical strength and high-temperature phase stability; synthesized from elemental powders by mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition reported as Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%) with the corresponding wt.% (Fe-46.00%, Mn-21.50%, Ni-18.13%, Al-8.34%, Si-5.78%, C-0.25%). Starting elemental powders were 99.2% pure. Theoretical density calculated by rule of mixture is 6.55 g/cc; measured density of SPSed pellet ~6.49±0.3 g/cc (relative density ~99%).

source.reason: The paper reports a single, specific non-equiatomic high entropy steel composition; the elemental powder was taken in the proportion Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%) (Fe-46.00%, Mn-21.50%, Ni-18.13%, Al-8.34%, Si-5.78%, C-0.25%; wt.%). All processing states (milling, annealing, SPS) share this same composition, so only one alloy is defined.

processes.description: Starting elemental powder blend of Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si and C in the HES proportion before any milling (0 h), showing XRD peaks of the individual elements.

source.reason: The XRD pattern of the pre-mixed powder of alloying elements at 0 h revealing the diffraction peaks of the individual elements is characterized (Fig. 1(a)); this is the starting reference state of the alloy before alloying.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed (planetary ball mill, 200 rpm, BPR 10:1, WC vials/balls, toluene) for 5 h; low intensity peaks of all the elements have vanished indicating the onset of alloying.
processes.processes_notes: Mechanical alloying performed in a planetary ball mill (Retsch PM 400/2) at 200 rpm with ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; milling stopped for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating.

source.reason: Phase evolution study reports that low intensity peaks of all the elements have vanished after 5 h of milling, defining this as a distinct milling-time state.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 10 h; SEM morphology and particle size distribution histogram recorded at this milling stage.

source.reason: SEM micrographs and particle size distribution histograms are reported for the powder milled at 10 h (Fig. 2(f)), making it a distinct characterized milling state.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 15 h; the intensity of Al diffraction peaks diminishes, indicating Al has the highest alloying rate.

source.reason: The phase evolution text explicitly describes that the intensity of Al diminishes after 15 h of milling, distinguishing this milling state.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 20 h; intense Ni and Mn peaks are no longer evident in the XRD pattern and particle size decreases drastically.

source.reason: Text reports that after 20 h the intense peaks of Ni and Mn are not evident and that the average particle size decreased drastically after 20 h of milling, defining a distinct state.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 25 h; solid solution formed with BCC (a = 0.286 nm) and gamma-brass type (a = 0.872 nm) phases; Rietveld phase fraction/crystallite size/dislocation density reported (Table 2).

source.reason: The paper states that the solid solution has been formed after 25 h of milling (BCC + gamma-brass type) and tabulates its phase fraction, crystallite size and dislocation density (Table 2).

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 30 h; BCC + gamma-brass type + residual Si phases; Rietveld phase fraction, crystallite size and dislocation density reported (Table 2) and particle size histogram (Fig. 2(h)).

source.reason: Table 2 tabulates the phase fraction, lattice strain, crystallite size and dislocation density for the 30 h milled powder, and Fig. 2(h) gives its particle size distribution, defining a distinct state.

processes.description: Powder mechanically alloyed for 35 h (the final as-milled state used for annealing and SPS); forms a multi-phase structure of BCC (major), gamma-brass type and partially ordered B2-type plus a trace of undissolved Si, with nanocrystalline grains (mean particle size 3-5 um, crystallite size ~10-17 nm).
processes.processes_notes: This is the reference as-milled state from which the annealed and SPSed samples are derived.

source.reason: The 35 h milled powder is the main as-milled research object; its multi-phase constitution, nanocrystalline structure and characterization (XRD Rietveld Fig. 1(c,d), TEM Fig. 3, EDS Table 3) are extensively reported.

processes.process_name: Annealed at 400 °C for 1 h then water quenched
processes.description: 35 h milled powder encapsulated in quartz tube under argon and annealed at 400 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching; phases BCC + gamma-brass type + B2 (Table 4).
processes.processes_notes: Annealing series carried out on the 35 h milled powder at 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C, each 1 h + water quenching, for thermal stability study.

source.reason: The paper annealed the 35 h milled sample for 1 h at 400 °C followed by water quenching and reports the resulting phase constitution, so this is a distinct heat-treated state.

processes.process_name: Annealed at 500 °C for 1 h then water quenched
processes.description: 35 h milled powder annealed at 500 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching; the alloy remains thermally stable (BCC + gamma-brass type + B2) at this temperature.
processes.processes_notes: Upper bound of thermal stability (~500 °C) of the milled powder.

source.reason: Anneal at 500 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching is a distinct condition; the paper reports the phases and states the milled powder is thermally stable up to ~500 °C.

processes.process_name: Annealed at 600 °C for 1 h then water quenched
processes.description: 35 h milled powder annealed at 600 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching; forms BCC + gamma-brass type + B2 + Fe5Si3-type silicide phase.

source.reason: Annealing at 600 °C is a distinct condition at which the Fe5Si3-type silicide phase is reported; Table 4 gives its phase fraction and lattice parameter.

processes.process_name: Annealed at 800 °C for 1 h then water quenched
processes.description: 35 h milled powder annealed at 800 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching; BCC + gamma-brass type + increased B2-type + Fe5Si3-type silicide, with no new phase change but an increased amount of B2.

source.reason: Annealing at 800 °C is a distinct condition; text states that at 800 °C no phase change occurred but the amount of B2-type phase increased, and Table 4 lists its phases.

processes.process_name: Spark plasma sintered at 900 °C, 50 MPa, 15 min
processes.description: 35 h milled powder consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 900 °C under 50 MPa with a heating rate of 100 °C/min and holding time of 15 min; retains BCC (major) + partially ordered B2 + trace gamma-brass type and forms Fe5Si3-type silicide, with relative density ~99%.
processes.processes_notes: The SPSed pellet (~30 mm diameter, ~9 mm thickness) was sectioned by wire EDM for microhardness and compression testing.

source.reason: The 35 h milled powder was consolidated by SPS at 900 °C, 50 MPa, 100 °C/min, 15 min; this is the final bulk research object on which mechanical properties were measured.

unmapped_findings: The paper reports measured properties of the SPSed HES: density ~6.49±0.3 g/cc (relative density ~99%, theoretical density 6.55 g/cc), microhardness ~7.8±0.3 GPa, elastic modulus ~184±5 GPa, ultimate compressive strength ~2046±160 MPa and compressive ductility ~19%.
Melting point of the HES composition was estimated as 1638 K (machine-learning approach) and 1620 K (rule of mixture).

Thermodynamic parameters of the non-equiatomic FeMnNiAlSiC HES: mixing enthalpy dHmix = -8.4 kJ/mol, configurational entropy dSconf = 12.4 J/K-mol, size mismatch delta = 7.6%, Omega = 2.4, VEC = 6.9 (predicted BCC/dual-phase).

CALPHAD (Thermo-Calc, TCFE8 database) property diagram and single-point equilibrium calculations predict phases from 25 °C to 1200 °C (liquid, BCC_A2#1, B2, BCC_A2#2, M3Si, BCC_A2#3); some differences vs experimental results attributed to the database used.

Strengthening mechanism analysis indicates grain-boundary (52.55%) and dislocation (30.00%) strengthening are dominant, with precipitation (5.70%) and solid-solution (6.14%) contributions; calculated theoretical strength 2164 MPa vs measured 2046 MPa.

Multiple other HEAs, high entropy steels and conventional steels (e.g., Fe40.4Ni11.3Mn34.8Al7.5Cr6, Fe40Mn40Co10Cr10, Cr20Mn10Fe35Ni35, Fe40Cr25Ni15Al15Co5, FeMnNiCrAlSi-C) are cited from earlier literature only for comparison/context and are not research objects of this study.
